issues.title: [Inductor] Correctness discrepancy in torch.minimum with signed zeros (-0.0 vs 0.0) on CUDA (bfloat16)
issues.author: xyt66665000
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

There is a correctness discrepancy between eager mode and `torch.compile` (Inductor) when calling `torch.minimum` with `-0.0` and `0.0` using `bfloat16` tensors on CUDA. 

Eager mode preserves the negative sign and returns `-0.0` (`0x8000`), whereas `torch.compile` returns `0.0` (`0x0000`).

### Reproduction Script
```python
import torch

def fn(x, y):
    return torch.minimum(x, y)

x = torch.tensor([-0.0], dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
y = torch.tensor([0.0], dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")

eager_out = fn(x, y)
inductor_fn = torch.compile(fn)
inductor_out = inductor_fn(x, y)

print("--- Output ---")
print(f"Eager:    {eager_out.item()} (Hex: {eager_out.view(torch.int16).item() & 0xFFFF:#06x})")
print(f"Inductor: {inductor_out.item()}  (Hex: {inductor_out.view(torch.int16).item() & 0xFFFF:#06x})")
```

### Actual Output
```text
(torch-nightly) xyt19@Oasis:/tmp$ python bug.py
--- Output ---
Eager:    -0.0 (Hex: 0x8000)
Inductor: 0.0  (Hex: 0x0000)
```

### Expected Behavior
`torch.compile` should match the eager mode output and return `-0.0` (Hex: `0x8000`).

issues.title: [DTensor] Gradient of unused output becomes plain torch.Tensor in backward, causing type mismatch with torch.compile
issues.author: fegin
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary**

When an op with DTensor inputs returns multiple DTensor outputs and one output is unused in the downstream computation, the gradient for that unused output is returned as a plain torch.Tensor of zeros instead of a DTensor. This causes a type mismatch during the backward pass when combined with torch.compile.

**Reproduce**

Mini repro: https://gist.github.com/fegin/ac5ded1a7bdb8686a94357043ef74b50

Command: `torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 dtensor_unused_output.py`

Error message:
```
[rank0]:   File "/data/users/chienchin/mywork3/pytorch/torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/runtime_wrappers.py", line 2526, in backward
[rank0]:     all_args = _backward_prologue_functional(
[rank0]:   File "/data/users/chienchin/mywork3/pytorch/torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/runtime_wrappers.py", line 1972, in _backward_prologue_functional
[rank0]:     flat_processed_tangents = list(
[rank0]:   File "/data/users/chienchin/mywork3/pytorch/torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/runtime_wrappers.py", line 1975, in <genexpr>
[rank0]:     AOTDispatchAutograd.process_runtime_tangent(
```

comments.author: bdhirsh
comments.body:
So the main problem is this is a shortcoming of the fact that compile tries really hard to support partial graphs + the fact that we trace out a backward graph "ahead-of-time". We need to choose between raising a hard error, or silently having worse performance.

In this particular repro, the error is coming up because:

(1) The repro does some forward compute involving `self.weight2`, but the output of that compute is **not** used to compute a loss. So we never actually need to compute any gradients for `self.weight2`

(2) there are a few graph breaks, due to the prints in `MultiOutputOp.backward`

(3) this causes `torch.compile` to generate a few partial graphs, instead of one larger graph of the model ([tlparse](https://manifold.edge.x2p.facebook.net/v0/read/tree/logs/hirsheybar/eaf04aa3-0089-4c46-9641-9b583cecacad/custom/rank_0/index.html?bucketName=tlparse_reports&apiKey=tlparse_reports-key&withPayload=1&timeoutMsec=10000#[0/0])).

(4) if you look at the generated backward graph for `[1/0]` ([link](https://manifold.edge.x2p.facebook.net/v0/read/tree/logs/hirsheybar/eaf04aa3-0089-4c46-9641-9b583cecacad/custom/rank_0/-_0_0_1/aot_backward_graph_10.txt?bucketName=tlparse_reports&apiKey=tlparse_reports-key&withPayload=1&timeoutMsec=10000)) `torch.compile` assumes that we need to compute gradients for **both** `self.weight1` and `self.weight2`, which requires running an extra matmul.

Running "additional matmuls", or "additional collectives" in the backward seems to me like a pretty unacceptable perf hit. The general way to avoid this performance hit is to:

(1) fix graph breaks

(2) ensure that if you return multiple outputs from a compiled region, then if you don't actually plan on computing gradients for all of the outputs, you should `.detach()` any outputs that you don't want to compute gradients for.

comments.author: bdhirsh
comments.body: My tentative vote would be to make this error more informative, rather than removing it (and creating performance cliffs). I have an issue here about improving the error message: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/172556

comments.author: fegin
comments.body: This is not a torch.compile issue. torch.compile just surface the error in a different way and is confusing. But the bug does exist even without torch.compile. We will get mix a torch.Tensor and DTensor error due to grad_output_2 being a plain Tensor.

comments.author: wconstab
comments.body:
Trying to catch up on this issue. It sounds like the situation is that we have inconsistent proposals between compile and eager. 

For compile, we could make it an error if you don't bprop through all the outputs of all the graphs that required grad. This would nicely avoid ever needing zeros like handling for subclasses, or wasting activation memory, or doing extra work in backwards.

But in eager, we can't error like this because we can't know if an output will be used later. And to be complete / correct in eager, we do need zeros like handling for subclasses.  Note, it's also better in eager to detach if possible, to avoid wasting memory.

It might be worth adding the subclass zeros like handling for eager, and erroring (or warning?) in compile, and making changes to add detach when possible in fsdp/cp apis?

issues.title: [inductor] TypeError: Too few arguments for CSE in cutedsl_kernel.py (torch 2.10.0, Python 3.11)
issues.author: swagglian
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug Report

### Summary

In `torch 2.10.0`, `torch/_inductor/codegen/cutedsl/cutedsl_kernel.py` references `CSE[Any]` with only one type argument, but the `CSE` class in `torch/_inductor/codegen/common.py` is defined as `Generic[CSEVariableType, AugmentedKeyT]`, which requires two type arguments. This causes a `TypeError` at import time on Python 3.11.

### Error Message

```
TypeError: Too few arguments for <class 'torch._inductor.codegen.common.CSE'>; actual 1, expected 2
```

Full traceback:
```
File ".../torch/_inductor/codegen/cutedsl/cutedsl_kernel.py", line 77, in CuteDSLSubgraphInfo
    cse: Optional[CSE[Any]] = None
         ~~~^^^^^
TypeError: Too few arguments for <class 'torch._inductor.codegen.common.CSE'>; actual 1, expected 2
```

### Root Cause

In `torch/_inductor/codegen/common.py`, the `CSE` class is defined with two generic parameters:

```python
# torch/_inductor/codegen/common.py, line 1886
class CSE(Generic[CSEVariableType, AugmentedKeyT]):
```

However, in `torch/_inductor/codegen/cutedsl/cutedsl_kernel.py`, it is used with only one type argument:

```python
# torch/_inductor/codegen/cutedsl/cutedsl_kernel.py, line 77
cse: Optional[CSE[Any]] = None
```

This internal inconsistency was introduced when `CSE` was refactored to accept a second generic parameter, but `cutedsl_kernel.py` was not updated accordingly.

Note: On Python 3.11, both `Optional[CSE[Any]]` and `CSE[Any] | None` trigger runtime generic type validation, so changing the annotation syntax alone does not fix the issue. The correct fix is:

```python
cse: Optional[CSE[Any, Any]] = None
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
python3 -c "from torch._inductor.codegen.cutedsl.cutedsl_kernel import CuteDSLTemplateKernel"
```

### Environment

- PyTorch version: 2.10.0+cpu
- Python version: 3.11.4
- OS: openEuler (aarch64)
- Install source: official wheel `torch-2.10.0+cpu-cp311-cp311-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl`

### Expected Behavior

The module imports successfully without any `TypeError`.

### Suggested Fix

In `torch/_inductor/codegen/cutedsl/cutedsl_kernel.py`, update the annotation:

```python
# Before
cse: Optional[CSE[Any]] = None

# After
cse: Optional[CSE[Any, Any]] = None
```

### Versions

https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/torch-2.10.0%2Bcpu-cp311-cp311-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl
